sources.citation: Wodtko, Dagmar S. 2021. Spelling Tartessian / De ortografía tartésica. Palaeohispanica 21, 219-234. DOI 10.36707/palaeohispanica.v21i0.411
sources.note: Corpus of attested consonant groups, word-boundary criteria (texts end in vowels, -n, possibly -ŕ), geminates, mute/redundant vowels, hypothetical spellings of stop+consonant clusters compared with Celtiberian practice. Nothing on accent or stress (the only 'stress' token is the verb 'This again stresses..').

sources.citation: Luján, Eugenio R. 2020. El sudoeste de la Península Ibérica. Palaeohispanica 20, 561-589. DOI 10.36707/palaeohispanica.v0i20.394
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.4 (pp. 568-570) gives five vowels, diphthongs, stop places, nasals, two sibilants, /l/, probably two rhotics, syllable types V, VR, CV, CVR (after De Hoz 2010), and stresses that the script is not fully deciphered and the language unidentified; no accent/stress statement anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent acento/acentua/prosod/tónica: zero hits).

sources.citation: Koch, John T. 2019. Common Ground and Progress on the Celtic of the South-western (SW) Inscriptions. Aberystwyth: University of Wales Centre for Advanced Welsh and Celtic Studies (Celtic Studies Publications), 131 pp. ISBN 978-1-907029-26-4.
sources.note: Historical-comparative commentary under the Celtic hypothesis: treatment of Proto-Celtic diphthongs, *u̯-, *(p), b/m alternation, syncope in individual etymologies, claim that the script was borrowed from a language phonologically like Iberian/Palaeo-Basque (no /m/, no /w/ sign). The only 'accent' token (s.v. kiielaoe) concerns a reconstructed Pre-Celtic movable accent in *kéilii̯o-/*kilii̯o-, not the SW language. No statement on Tartessian word accent in 131 pp. (a full-text search for stress/accent/stress/prosod/penult/tonic).

sources.citation: Mikhailova, Tatyana A. 2015. Celtic origin: location in time and space? Reconsidering the 'East-West Celtic' debate. Journal of Language Relationship / Вопросы языкового родства 13(3-4), 257-279.
sources.note: Review-discussion of Koch's and Kaufman's Celtic readings; no phonological description, no accent/stress mention (full text searched online: accent 0, stress 1 = verb).

sources.citation: Rodríguez Ramos, Jesús. 2015. De nuevo sobre la lectura de la escritura monumental tartesia o sudlusitana. Veleia 32, 125-150. DOI 10.1387/veleia.14983
sources.note: Four reading problems: Algarve variant heth-signs = ta; readings of ku and pu; a fourth sign tied to vowel u; whether /m/ was written (n-like and my-like signs, np digraphs, nb/b alternations), with the suggestion that syllable-finally only a dental nasal archiphoneme existed and the observation that /a/ predominates and /e/ is scarce in first syllables of both Baetican toponyms and the stelae. Nothing on accent, stress, vowel quantity or tone (a full-text search for stress/accent acent/prosod/tonic/stress: 0 hits).

sources.citation: Correia, Virgílio Hipólito. 2014. A escrita do Sudoeste da Península Ibérica: velhos dados, novas teorias e a sua importância para o estudo das antigas culturas hispânicas. Portugalia, Nova Série 35, 77-93. Porto: DCTP-FLUP.
sources.note: 18-page Portuguese review (sections: Origem dos estudos; Problemas de epigrafia e arqueologia; A investigacao sobre a epigrafia do Sudoeste; O problema do signario; A evolucao da escrita; Os problemas de leitura; A integracao historico-cultural da escrita do Sudoeste). Treats the script as a semi-syllabary adapted from Phoenician, sign delimitation and phonetic values, the poverty of the lexical material ('uma duzia de elementos lexicais'), anthroponymy, and the Celtic-from-the-West debate. a full-text search for stress/accent acent|prosod|tonic|aton|silaba tonica|entoa|tonal|tom|quantidade|v…

sources.note: No statement on word stress of the stelae language. Only fn. 39 (p. 302) remarks that first-syllable accent of the Latinized Turdetanian toponym Munigua is deducible from its Romance outcome Mulva -- a single toponym, not a rule for the language.

sources.note: Nothing; comparative/etymological argument for Celtic affiliation, no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Koch, John T. 2008 [PDF created 2009]. Aberystwyth: University of Wales Centre for Advanced Welsh and Celtic Studies, 18 pp. (web PDF).
sources.note: Script facts (no voice distinction in stops; vowel-conditioned stop letters 'broadly reminiscent of the sound system of Goidelic'), then Celtic etymologies of SW forms. No accent/stress/syllable statement (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).

sources.citation: Valério, Miguel. 2008. Origin and development of the Paleohispanic scripts: the orthography and phonology of the Southwestern alphabet. Revista Portuguesa de Arqueologia 11(2), 107-138.
sources.note: Derives the SW script from Phoenician; reconstructs a 29-sign system: 5 vowels, 3 stop series x 5 vowel-bound signs, 9 free consonant letters; discusses vocalic redundancy, absence of voice distinction, rare letters. No statement on stress/accent of the SW language; endnote 9 speculates that Iberian word-final stops may result from 'accent-driven loss of final vowels' (another language).

sources.citation: Rodríguez Ramos, Jesús. 2002. Las inscripciones sudlusitano-tartesias: su función, lengua y contexto socio-económico. Complutum 13, 85-95.
sources.note: Language section weighs the Celtic vs Anatolian vs unknown-IE hypotheses from the formula words (naŕkeenii, baare), vowel statistics (scarcity of e, frequency of a, e mostly in first syllables), and states the script renders the language 'sílaba a sílaba' through the pseudo-syllabograms; nothing on accent/stress.

sources.citation: Rodríguez Ramos, Jesús. 2000. La lectura de las inscripciones sudlusitano-tartesias. Faventia 22/1, 21-48. Bellaterra: Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona.
sources.note: 28-page critical revision of the transcription system sign by sign (heth-shaped signs, S-102 as a variant of ke, a possible square-i variant for a semiconsonant /y/, possible palatalization after Correa 1992, vowel redundancy of the pseudo-syllabograms, preponderance of /a/). Full-text search acent/prosod/tonic/silaba/cantidad: no statement on word accent, stress, quantity or tone of the language; the phonetic remarks concern segment values of signs only.

sources.citation: Rodríguez Ramos, Jesús. 2000. Sobre la geminación gráfica de signos vocálicos en la escritura sudlusitano-tartesia. Veleia 17, 147-152.
sources.note: The one study of the only graphic phenomenon that could in principle encode prosody (doubled vowel signs). Conclusion: two orthographic rules of some stone-cutters - a vowel is doubled before tautosyllabic r (unless preceded by a stop sign or o/u), and every absolute-final i is doubled (unless preceded by a stop sign); possibly word-initial o. Quotes Correa 1993 that doubling 'podrían deberse, tal vez, a normas gráficas desconocidas (representación de cantidad, etc.) o al encuentro de morfemas'; leaves open whether doubling before r reflects phonetic lengthening. Accent is never invoked.
